subject.title: fix: unify macos dashboard auth startup

question: Should macOS Dashboard browser auth ever receive native/stored device tokens, or should injected browser auth be limited to configured shared token/password only?
rationale: The PR fixes one reported parity bug by expanding native-token use, while the related security report asks for the opposite boundary; code review cannot safely choose that credential policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Limit browser injection to shared auth
options.body: Update this PR or replace it so the Dashboard browser receives only configured shared token/password while preserving shared presentation construction where safe.

options.title: Accept native-token parity
options.body: Keep native/stored device tokens in browser Dashboard auth, but require explicit security approval, docs/tests for that contract, and macOS runtime proof.

options.title: Pause conflicting drafts
options.body: Hold or close this PR and the sibling draft until maintainers choose one Dashboard auth policy and one implementation path.

recommendation.title: Limit browser injection to shared auth
recommendation.body: Update this PR or replace it so the Dashboard browser receives only configured shared token/password while preserving shared presentation construction where safe.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available history around Dashboard token handling and public auth docs, which is the boundary this PR changes.
